title: A Border Gateway Protocol 4 (BGP-4)

hero.subtitle: The routing protocol that holds the Internet together

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
BGP-4 is the de facto standard exterior gateway protocol of the Internet. It enables autonomous systems (ASes) to exchange reachability information for IP prefixes, forming the global Internet routing table.

BGP is fundamentally a policy-based routing protocol. Unlike IGPs that optimize for shortest path, BGP allows network operators to implement complex routing policies based on business relationships, peering agreements, and traffic engineering goals.

BGP uses TCP (port 179) as its transport, ensuring reliable delivery of routing updates. The protocol is incremental - after the initial exchange of the full routing table, only changes are propagated.
sections.eli5: The Internet is like many countries that each run their own roads. BGP is how neighbouring countries tell each other which cities they can reach, so a letter can cross several countries to get there.

sections.title: Protocol Overview
sections.content:
BGP is a path-vector protocol. Each route advertisement carries the complete AS path it has traversed, enabling loop detection and policy-based route selection.

OPENEstablishes BGP session and exchanges session parameters
UPDATEAdvertises new routes or withdraws previously announced routes
KEEPALIVEMaintains session liveness (sent often enough that the Hold Timer never expires; the RFC suggests at most one third of the Hold Time, whose suggested default is 90 seconds)
NOTIFICATIONReports errors and terminates the session
sections.eli5: Each route in BGP comes with the list of countries it passed through, so nobody sends a letter around in circles. Routers talk using four kinds of message: hello, news, "still here" and "I am hanging up".

sections.title: Path Attributes
sections.content:
Each BGP UPDATE message carries a set of path attributes that describe the properties of the advertised routes. These attributes drive the route selection process.

AS_PATHOrdered list of ASes the route has traversed (loop detection)Well-known mandatory
NEXT_HOPIP address of the next-hop router for the advertised prefixWell-known mandatory
LOCAL_PREFPreference value within an AS (higher = preferred)Well-known
MEDMulti-Exit Discriminator - suggests preferred entry point (lower = preferred)Optional non-transitive
COMMUNITYTags for implementing routing policies (e.g., no-export)Optional transitive
ORIGINOrigin of the route: IGP, EGP, or IncompleteWell-known mandatory
sections.eli5: Each route comes with sticky notes that describe it: who it came through, where to send the mail next, and how much the sender likes it.

sections.title: Decision Process
sections.content:
When multiple paths exist to the same destination, BGP uses a well-defined decision process to select the best path. Attributes are compared in strict order of priority.

1. Highest LOCAL_PREF
Prefer routes with the highest local preference value (iBGP only).
2. Shortest AS_PATH
Prefer routes that traverse the fewest autonomous systems.
3. Lowest ORIGIN
Prefer IGP over EGP over Incomplete origin types.
4. Lowest MED
Prefer the path with the lowest multi-exit discriminator (same neighbor AS).
5. eBGP over iBGP
Prefer externally learned routes over internally learned ones.
6. Lowest IGP Cost
Prefer the path with the lowest IGP metric to the next hop (hot potato routing).
sections.eli5: When there are several roads to the same city, the router runs through a checklist in the same order every time: the road I like most, the one with the fewest border crossings, and so on, until only one road is left.

sections.title: UPDATE Message
sections.content:
The UPDATE message is the core of BGP routing information exchange. Each message can simultaneously withdraw previously advertised routes and advertise new ones.

BGP UPDATE Message
+-----------------------------------------------------+
|   Withdrawn Routes Length (2 octets)                |
+-----------------------------------------------------+
|   Withdrawn Routes (variable)                       |
+-----------------------------------------------------+
|   Total Path Attribute Length (2 octets)             |
+-----------------------------------------------------+
|   Path Attributes (variable)                        |
+-----------------------------------------------------+
|   Network Layer Reachability Information (variable)  |
+-----------------------------------------------------+

NLRI (Network Layer Reachability Information) encodes IP prefixes using a length-prefix pair, allowing efficient representation of routes ranging from /0 (default) to /32 (host routes).
sections.eli5: The news message can say "I can no longer reach these places" and "I can reach these new places, and here is how" in the same note.

sections.title: Finite State Machine
sections.content:
The BGP Finite State Machine (FSM) defines the lifecycle of a BGP session, from initial connection to established state and error handling.

IdleInitial state; no connection attempt in progress
ConnectTCP connection in progress to the peer
ActiveListening for TCP connection from the peer
OpenSentOPEN message sent; awaiting peer OPEN
OpenConfirmOPEN received; awaiting KEEPALIVE
EstablishedSession is up; UPDATE messages can be exchanged

A BGP session stuck in the Active state usually indicates a connectivity problem or misconfiguration. This is one of the most common troubleshooting scenarios in BGP operations.
sections.eli5: A BGP conversation goes through steps: stand by, knock on the door, say hello, wait for hello back, and finally chat. If anything goes wrong, it goes back to standing by.

subtitle: The routing protocol that holds the Internet together

tldr.problem: The Internet is thousands of independently run networks, and each must tell its neighbours which addresses it can reach without any central map.
tldr.mechanism: Neighbouring routers open a TCP session on port 179 and exchange OPEN, UPDATE, KEEPALIVE and NOTIFICATION messages. Each route carries its AS path and other attributes, and every router applies local policy to pick one best path per prefix.
tldr.outcome: The one routing protocol that joins every autonomous system, extended since (4-byte AS numbers, multiprotocol support, communities) but never replaced.

eli5.summary: The Internet is a huge number of separate networks, and BGP is how they tell each other which streets they can reach. Each network passes along the list of networks a message would cross, and picks the route it likes best.

questions: how does bgp choose the best path
what are the bgp session states
what is the difference between ibgp and ebgp
today: BGP-4 is still the only inter-domain routing protocol in use, and RFC 4271 is still the base specification. Real deployments add to it: 4-byte AS numbers (RFC 6793), multiprotocol extensions for IPv6 and VPNs (RFC 4760), and communities (RFC 1997). Route origin validation with RPKI is used to address the lack of any built-in check that an AS may originate a prefix. Common open-source implementations include BIRD, FRRouting and OpenBGPD.

fields.name: Marker
fields.desc: 16 octets, included for compatibility. MUST be set to all ones.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Total length of the message in octets, including the header. At least 19 and no greater than 4096.

fields.name: Type
fields.desc: Message type code: 1 OPEN, 2 UPDATE, 3 NOTIFICATION, 4 KEEPALIVE.

viz.caption: FIG 2.2 · OPEN MESSAGE · 10 FIXED BYTES AFTER THE HEADER

fields.name: Version
fields.desc: BGP protocol version number. The current version is 4.

fields.name: My Autonomous System
fields.desc: The AS number of the sender (2 octets in this RFC).

fields.name: Hold Time
fields.desc: Seconds the sender proposes for the Hold Timer. The smaller of the two proposals is used. Must be zero or at least 3.

fields.name: BGP Identifier
fields.desc: An IP address assigned to the sender, chosen at startup and used for every interface and peer.

fields.name: Opt Parm Len
fields.desc: Length of the Optional Parameters field in octets. Zero means none.

viz.caption: Attribute type codes defined in RFC 4271 §4.3

data.title: How a prefix is encoded in NLRI (192.0.2.0/24 as an example)
data.code:
+---------------------------+
|   Length (1 octet)        |   length of the prefix in bits
+---------------------------+
|   Prefix (variable)       |   just enough octets to hold those bits
+---------------------------+

192.0.2.0/24  ->  0x18  C0 00 02
                  (24 bits = 3 prefix octets)
0.0.0.0/0     ->  0x00
                  (length zero matches all addresses; no prefix octets)

messages.label: TCP connect to port 179
messages.note: Either side may open the connection; the peer listens on port 179.

messages.label: OPEN
messages.note: Version 4, AS number, Hold Time, BGP Identifier.

messages.label: OPEN
messages.note: The smaller of the two Hold Times is used.

messages.label: UPDATE
messages.note: Advertises a prefix with its path attributes.

messages.label: KEEPALIVE
messages.note: Sent periodically, at most every third of the Hold Time, so the Hold Timer does not expire.

messages.label: NOTIFICATION
messages.note: Sent when an error is found, for example Hold Timer Expired. The connection is closed immediately afterwards.
